mainTopic: Hearing and הפרה: whether a חרש can cancel his wife's נדרים, and whether a husband can cancel the vows of two wives at once
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. A husband had told his steward to cancel his wife's future vows, and this was brought as a proof that a בעל can cancel without hearing. The גמרא pushes the proof away: the husband meant the vows would be cancelled once he hears them, and he set it up early in case he is too busy then. So it remains unproven whether a hearing husband can cancel without hearing. Next, רמי בר חמא asks whether a חרש, who cannot hear at all, can cancel his wife's vows. He suggests רבי זירא's rule about mixing a מנחה: a step that is normally not required becomes required when it is impossible to do. רבא answers from a ברייתא that reads 'and her husband hears' as excluding the wife of a חרש, so a חרש cannot cancel. Then the גמרא asks whether a husband can cancel the vows of two wives at once, since the פסוק uses the singular word ״אותה״. רבינא brings a ברייתא about two סוטות, where רבי יהודה reads ״והשקה״ as 'her, by herself,' suggesting that each wife needs her own הפרה.

steps.title: The steward case does not prove cancelling without hearing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the steward case. The husband meant that the vows would be cancelled once he hears them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the husband said to the steward: 'When I hear the vow, it will be cancelled for her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away an earlier proof that a בעל can cancel vows without hearing them. It explains that in the steward case the husband set up the cancellation to take effect only when he hears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof assumed the husband cancelled vows he never heard. The גמרא reads the case differently: the הפרה kicks in at the moment he hears. So hearing is still part of the picture, and nothing is proven.

keyTerms.meaning: here too, the same is true here
when I hear
it is cancelled for her

phrases.english: Here too, it is where he said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the steward from the case the גמרא quoted just before this.

phrases.english: When I hear, it will be cancelled for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a proof brought just before this section, from the steward case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the steward case that a husband can cancel without hearing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case can be read as a cancellation that takes effect only once the husband hears, so it shows nothing about cancelling without hearing.

steps.title: Why not just cancel when he hears?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the husband would set this up in advance at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he hears, let him cancel it then!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading of the steward case. If he will hear the vow anyway, why arrange the cancellation ahead of time?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting things up early only makes sense if hearing is not needed. If the husband has to hear anyway, the advance arrangement looks pointless. This puts pressure on the answer from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: let him cancel it for her

phrases.english: When he hears, let him cancel it for her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the husband meant 'when I hear, it is cancelled.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he has to hear the vow anyway, he could just cancel it then. The advance arrangement would serve no purpose.

steps.title: He worried he might be too busy
steps.stepSummary: The husband set it up early because he feared he would be busy and forget to cancel when he heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought: perhaps I will be preoccupied at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 2. The husband arranged things early so the cancellation would happen on its own even if he was busy when he heard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The advance arrangement does have a purpose: it protects against forgetting. That keeps the reading of step 1 standing, so the steward case still does not prove that a בעל can cancel without hearing. The question is left unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: he thought, he reasoned
I will be preoccupied or busy

steps.whatToRemember: The steward case is pushed away: the husband set up a cancellation that takes effect when he hears, in case he is too busy then. So it remains unproven whether a בעל can cancel without hearing.

phrases.english: He thought: perhaps I will be preoccupied.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a practical reason for the arrangement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Setting up the cancellation early seemed pointless if he had to hear anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: It protects against forgetting while busy, so the reading 'cancelled when I hear' holds.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא asks about a חרש husband
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks whether a חרש can cancel his wife's vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: A deaf man, can he cancel vows for his wife?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רמי בר חמא asks whether a husband who cannot hear at all can perform הפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the last discussion. That one asked about a husband who can hear but did not. This asks about one who is not able to hear at all.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked (a real question needing an answer)
a deaf man
that he cancel (a vow)

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
A deaf man, what is the law, may he cancel for his wife?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question related to the hearing discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a חרש is able to cancel his wife's vows.

steps.title: First side: a deaf man may be different
steps.stepSummary: Even if a hearing husband can cancel without hearing, a חרש might be different, because for him hearing is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say a husband can cancel without hearing, that is because he is able to hear. But a deaf man, who is not able to hear, may fall under רבי זירא's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא explains why his question is a real question. He lays out the reason a חרש might not be able to cancel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not hearing is one thing; being unable to hear is another. A missing step can be overlooked when it could have been done. When it cannot be done at all, it may hold the whole thing back. That is the idea he takes from רבי זירא.

keyTerms.meaning: if you were to say, even if you decide
someone able to hear
this is the same as

steps.confusionAlert: He is not saying a hearing husband definitely CAN cancel without hearing. That question was left open. He is saying: even if that were allowed, a חרש might still not be able to cancel.

phrases.english: If you were to say
a husband can cancel without hearing,
that is because he is able to hear.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חֵרֵשׁ דְּלָאו בַּר מִישְׁמַע הוּא,
phrases.english: But a deaf man, who is not able to hear,
this is the rule of Rabbi Zeira.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר בַּעַל מֵיפֵר בְּלֹא שְׁמִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the question asked in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether being unable to hear, as opposed to simply not hearing, blocks הפרה.

steps.title: רבי זירא's rule about mixing a meal-offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא: if flour can be mixed with oil, failing to mix does not ruin the מנחה. If it cannot be mixed, the mixing holds it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי זירא said: Whatever is fit for mixing, the mixing does not hold it back. Whatever is not fit for mixing, the mixing does hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי זירא's rule, which רמי בר חמא just mentioned. This is the background for the first side of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mixing oil into a מנחה is normally not required after the fact. If it is impossible to mix, the מנחה is not valid. Applied to our case: a hearing husband who did not hear might still cancel, but a חרש who cannot hear might not.

keyTerms.meaning: mixing (the flour of a מנחה with oil)
fit, able to be done
holds back, makes it invalid if missing

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי זירא's rule is a general principle that the גמרא uses in many places: being able to do something matters, even when actually doing it is not required.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Zeira said:
Whatever is fit for mixing,
phrases.notes: He is talking about flour of a מנחה that can be mixed with its oil.

phrases.english: the mixing does not hold it back.
And whatever is not fit for mixing,
the mixing does hold it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the rule mentioned in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A step that is not required after the fact becomes required when it is impossible to do.

steps.title: Second side: maybe hearing is not required at all
steps.stepSummary: Or perhaps the words 'and her husband hears' do not make hearing required, so even a חרש can cancel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps 'and her husband hears' does not hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא gives the other side of his question. Maybe the פסוק's mention of hearing is not a requirement, so a חרש could also cancel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the words 'and her husband hears' only describe the usual situation, then hearing is not needed. In that case רבי זירא's rule does not apply, and a חרש can cancel.

keyTerms.meaning: or perhaps
and her husband hears (words of the פסוק)
does not hold it back, is not required

phrases.english: Or perhaps 'and her husband hears' does not hold it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא: וְשָׁמַע אִישָׁהּ לָא מְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side to step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the פסוק's mention of hearing is a real requirement.

steps.title: רבא brings a ברייתא excluding a deaf man's wife
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא: 'and her husband hears' excludes the wife of a חרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear: 'And her husband hears' excludes the wife of a deaf man.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רמי בר חמא's question with a ברייתא. It reads the פסוק as leaving out a deaf husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the word 'hears' as a real limit. A husband who cannot hear is outside the rule, so a חרש cannot cancel his wife's vows. This supports the first side of the question.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (a source that answers the question)
to exclude, leaving out
the wife of a deaf man

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
'And her husband hears' excludes the wife of a deaf man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question laid out in steps 4 through 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא reads 'and her husband hears' as excluding a חרש, so he cannot cancel.

steps.title: Conclusion: a deaf man cannot cancel his wife's vows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof: a חרש cannot perform הפרה for his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבא's proof and closes the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing is required at least to the point that a husband who is not able to hear cannot cancel. The proof comes straight from the ברייתא's reading of the פסוק. It does not settle whether a hearing husband can cancel without hearing.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from this, it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: A חרש cannot cancel his wife's vows. The ברייתא learns this from 'and her husband hears,' which excludes the wife of a deaf man.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A חרש cannot perform הפרה on his wife's vows.

steps.title: Can a husband cancel vows for two wives at once?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a husband can do הפרה for two wives at the same time, or whether the word ״אותה״ limits him to one wife at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Can a husband cancel the vows of his two wives at the same time? Is the word 'her' meant exactly (only one woman), or not exactly?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Can one act of הפרה work for two wives together?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about הפרה uses the singular word ״אותה״, 'her.' If that word is exact, each wife needs her own separate הפרה. If it is not exact, one statement could cancel both wives' נדרים.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before the חכמים
At the same time, in one act
'Her', a singular word in the פסוק
Exact, meant precisely
Not exact, not meant to limit

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
A husband, what is the law, may he cancel
for his two wives at the same time?
Is 'her' meant exactly, or not exactly?
phrases.notes: במדבר 30:9: ״ואם ביום שמע אישה יניא אותה״. The word 'her' there is singular.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about הפרה, after the discussion of a חרש ended in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the singular ״אותה״ mean a husband must do הפרה for each wife separately, or can he cancel both wives' vows together?

steps.title: רבינא brings a ברייתא about two סוטות
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes a ברייתא: two סוטות are not given the water to drink together, because each one feels bold with the other there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Come and hear: We do not give two סוטות the water to drink together, because each one's heart feels bold in front of the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא starts bringing a source to answer the question. This first opinion is the setup. The real proof comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא gives a practical reason for keeping two סוטות apart. If a woman has her friend beside her, she feels bolder and is less likely to admit what she did. This reason has nothing to do with the wording of a פסוק, so by itself it does not answer the question about ״אותה״.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, used to bring a proof
Give to drink (the bitter waters)
A woman suspected by her husband of adultery
Her heart is bold, so she does not feel humble

phrases.english: Ravina said: Come and hear:
We do not give two sotah women to drink together,
because her heart is bold in the presence of her friend.
phrases.notes: With another woman beside her, she won't feel embarrassed enough to admit guilt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question from step 10 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about giving the water to two סוטות

steps.title: רבי יהודה reads ״והשקה״ as 'her, by herself'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the reason is not the woman's boldness. The פסוק ״והשקה״ (her) means each woman drinks alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: That is not the reason. It is because the פסוק says 'and he shall make her drink.' 'Her' means her alone.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of רבינא's proof. רבי יהודה learns from the singular word 'her' in the פסוק of סוטה that only one woman may be involved at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats the singular 'her' as exact. It means one woman by herself. The word ״אותה״ in the פסוק of הפרה is also singular. So by the same reading, a husband should not be able to cancel two wives' נדרים in one act.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not for that reason
'And he shall make her drink' (במדבר 5:27)
By herself, alone

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, a singular word like 'her' in a פסוק can mean 'only one woman at a time.' רבינא uses this to suggest that הפרה must be done separately for each wife.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof comes from רבי יהודה's reason, not from the first opinion. The first opinion's reason is about the woman's boldness, and it says nothing about how to read the word 'her.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
This is not for that reason,
but because it is stated: 'And he shall make her drink'
meaning her, by herself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִן הַשֵּׁם הוּא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from step 11 with רבי יהודה's view, which is the part that supplies the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That ״אותה״ in הפרה means exactly one wife
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's reading of ״והשקה״ as 'her, by herself'
